checks.claim: C1: Section 2 handles the generic family in d=1,2,3 with a common unit H1 negative trial. It covers the source map, the common H1 closed coercive form and PDE domain identification, a negative bottom before conditional Teschl 10.13, E1/E2 with threshold 0, the max-min Lipschitz bound (4), the gap Delta>0 and the rate gap (5) including mu=0.
checks.reason: Source map: the images confirm Teschl 2nd ed. GSM157. Thm 10.2 (p258) gives the H2 domain, self-adjointness, lower bound, sigma_ess=[0,inf) and the C_c^inf core for V=-V_sigma, which is real and bounded. Thm 10.13 (p273) is conditional ('If E0=min sigma(H) is an eigenvalue'). Thm 4.12 (p141) allows the form domain and uses inf sigma_ess once eigenvalues run out. Cor 4.13 is on the same page. Form: with c=1+M we have 1<=c-V<=c, so q+c||.||^2 lies between ||u||_H1^2 and c||u||_H1^2. The Riesz plus elliptic H2 regularity argument is valid. Bottom: q>=-M for unit u, and the trial gives E1<=-eps<0=inf sigma_ess. So E1 is an isolated eigenvalue of finite multiplicity before 10.13 is applied, which is the correct order. E2 is either the next eigenvalue (distinct by simplicity) or the threshold 0, so E1<E2<=0. The bound |q_sigma-q_tau|<=dV on unit vectors passes through the inf and sup in 4.12, and this covers threshold crossings. lambda-mu=(E2-E1)/(lambda+mu)>=Delta/(2 sqrt M) because mu<=lambda<=sqrt M. There is no division by mu.

checks.claim: C2: L2 continuity of the positive ground state (6) via Rayleigh/orthogonal energy gap with a>0, then H2 continuity via eigen-equation (7); real choice and uniform bounds.
checks.reason: Hand-checked. First, q_sigma(p_tau)<=E1(tau)+dV<=E1(sigma)+2dV. The cross term vanishes because p_sigma is an eigenfunction. The spectral support of r (orthogonal to p_sigma) lies in [E2,inf), because below E2 the only spectrum is the simple E1. This gives q_sigma(p_tau)>=E1+(E2-E1)||r||^2, using a^2+||r||^2=1. Next, a=<p_tau,p_sigma> is positive since both functions are positive a.e., and a<=1 by Cauchy-Schwarz. Then ||p_tau-p_sigma||^2=2(1-a)<=2(1-a^2)=2||r||^2<=4dV/Delta. Finally, (1-Delta)p=(1-lambda^2+V)p is correct since -Delta p=(E1+V)p. The right side is L2-continuous and bounded by 1+2M, and the Bessel inverse is an isometry from L2 onto H2. The real representative is fixed by simplicity, conjugation invariance and positivity.

checks.claim: C3: fractional global-E identification (8)-(10), covering resolvent variational order, the scalar integral with Tonelli square root and domain inclusions, H^{1/2} quarter-domain, H^{-1/2} dual completion, no hidden n-dependence and no invalid power monotonicity.
checks.reason: Order: B<=A<=cB on H1 holds because 1<=c-V<=c and c>=1. The resolvent quadratic form is the supremum over the common form domain of 2Re<f,u>-q_T(u)-t||u||^2, so T<=S implies (T+t)^-1>=(S+t)^-1. Integral: substituting t=x r^2 gives (1/pi) * 2 sqrt(x) * (pi/2) = sqrt(x), which is correct. Tonelli on spectral measures, with values in [0,inf], gives T^{1/2}<=S^{1/2} as forms, including D(S^{1/4}) contained in D(T^{1/4}). Hence ||B^{1/4}u||<=||A^{1/4}u||<=c^{1/4}||B^{1/4}u||, and B^{1/4} is the H^{1/2} Bessel norm. Duality: for z in L2, the dual norm equals ||A^{-1/4}z||, attained at u proportional to A^{-1/2}z. Completion then gives an equivalent H^{-1/2} norm with constants c^{-1/4} and 1. The argument is dimension-free, and only the proved square-root form comparison is used.

checks.claim: C4: spectral wave calculus (11) on the Q^sp phase, including h=0 and mu=0 and all four weighted entries. The decaying ground branch is retained and Pi^E norms are bounded via c-lambda^2 and l, Lambda. The spectral flow is identified with the physical P^E through H2xH1, the strong-generator derivative, Duhamel plus Gronwall uniqueness, and density in global E only.
checks.reason: Weighted entries: C_t, sqrt(h+c)S_t, -hS_t/sqrt(h+c), C_t. For h>=0: |S_t|<=min(t,h^-1/2), the upper entry is at most sqrt(1+c)max(t,1), and the lower entry is at most 1. For -mu^2<=h<0: cosh<=e^{mu t}, sinh(ts)/s is the integral of cosh(rs) over [0,t] and so at most t e^{mu t}, |h|<=M and 1<=h+c<=c. These bounds hold at mu=0. Ground phase: (p,lambda p) gives 1 under ell^E, and (p,-lambda p) gives 0. Norm of e^E in E_sigma: Ap=(c-lambda^2)p with 1<=c-lambda^2<=c and lambda>=l. I verified (13) by direct cosh/sinh computation. Graph-level equivalence: ||Au|| and ||(1-Delta)u|| differ by at most M||u||, and A>=1, so the H2xH1 regularity is valid. Differentiating S_E(-t)X(t) gives the force (0,V u). Uniqueness holds because V maps H^{1/2} to L2 to H^{-1/2} with bound M. Density of C_c^inf x C_c^inf in E, with fixed-horizon bounds, extends equality to E. No density of E in F is used. The physical P^E rests on the named accepted base (fixed-mask note Sections 5 and 7, with (8) keeping iE invariant).

checks.claim: C5: full-F physical block (14) with C(t) and the actual D_sigma forcing; functional (15)-(17) with finite positive f=int Vp/(2lambda) and no p in L1; two-sided commutation, normalization, parameter continuity, and positive uniform margins for e0 and O_phi.
checks.reason: Block (14): the constant block follows from accepted (8) and S_F. The E component is the variation-of-constants solution of Y=S_E e+int S_E(t-r)[B^E Y+D C(r)c]. I checked by Fubini that P^E plus the forcing integral solves this. That step is stated but not displayed (see minor). Uniqueness then follows from (2). Constant functional: f is finite by L2 Cauchy-Schwarz, and positive because V is nonzero (from (1)) and continuous, V>=0 and p>0 a.e. ell^E(0,Vc1)=f c1, so the generator conditions give alpha=f/lambda and beta=f/lambda^2. The two integrals in (16) evaluate correctly, and the finite part combines with the tail to give ell P(t)=e^{lambda t}ell. Also ell(e_sigma)=1, P(t)e_sigma=e^{lambda t}e_sigma, ell(e0)=f/lambda>0 and O_phi(e_sigma)=int phi p>0. All are continuous in sigma, so compactness of I gives uniform minima. Positivity is used only a.e. inside integrals. The finite rational control matches: entrance beta/(2lambda^2) and wrong-projection defect beta/(2lambda).

checks.claim: C6: complement decomposition (18) with subtraction of the growing response to constant forcing; the t+t^2+t^3/6 integral; the (1+t)^3 e^{mu t} bound and eta<d0; the statewise Duhamel difference and Gronwall parameter bound (20) with measurable operator norm, with no operator-norm time continuity and no B(F)-valued RNP.
checks.reason: (18): Q(e,c)=(Q^E e-ell^C(c)e^E,c). Splitting D=Q^E D+e^E ell^E D and using (16), the e^E pieces combine to -e^E ell^C(C(t)c). This is exact. ||Q^E D C(r)||<=C(1+r), and the integrand is (1+t)+tr-r^2, whose integral is t+t^2+t^3/6. The remaining terms are bounded by C(1+t)e^{mu t}||e|| and C(1+t)|c|. With mu>=0 this gives (19). Since lambda-mu>=d0, any eta<d0 (and so eta<inf lambda) works. (20): the difference identity S_F B_sigma D + S_F(B_sigma-B_tau)P_tau is correct, and d_st follows from linearity in (2). The operator norm is a countable supremum over a dense subset of the unit sphere of continuous functions, so it is lower semicontinuous and measurable. Scalar Gronwall is therefore valid. No operator-norm derivative is used.

checks.claim: C7: for the actual original positive Psi (not only products): mean/covariance identity (21), finite raw variance (22) via local compact Gamma mass and a<1, Gamma(B1)>0 by homogeneity, positive correlation Q, v>=Q and h>=Gamma*q_avg for all sigma including 0, no global decay assumption, smooth mean (24) by differentiating the zero-extended test, mask applied after convolution, and no masked covariance replacing the raw cost.
checks.reason: The original model is Cov=|s-t|^{-a}Gamma, and h_s pairs with it by absolute Fubini on compact sets. Finiteness: for x and x-z in B_A we get |z|<=2A, so the spatial integral is at most ||Psi||^2|B_A|Gamma(B_2A). The time integral of |sigma-u|^-a over the unit square is 2/((1-a)(2-a)), which I verified. Positivity: Gamma(B1)=r^{alpha-d}Gamma(B_r) follows from Gamma(cA)=c^{d-alpha}Gamma(A), and this also holds at the white endpoint alpha=d=1. Q_z is continuous with Q_0>0, so Q(q_avg)>=(Q_0/2)Gamma(B_rho)>0. Since |sigma-u|^-a>=1 on [0,1]^2, positive Tonelli gives h_sigma>=Gamma*q_avg, and v>=int q_avg(Gamma*q_avg)=Q. Smoothness: after the substitution u=s-r, derivatives fall on Psi. The r and z ranges are bounded, and |r|^-a is integrable, so dominated differentiation is valid. Lipschitz continuity of V_sigma=m_R h_sigma in sup and L2 norms follows for fixed R. Z and v are fixed before the mask is chosen.

checks.claim: C8: common wide unit trial (25)-(26): plateau psi supported in B2 with psi>=c0 on B1, L>=2A, R>=2L, shifted-ball inclusion, Tonelli, Gamma mass, C_G constant and alpha<2, with Psi, Z and v fixed. Positive lambda and the Lipschitz rate (27) are defined only after R and eps_R are fixed. Additional tests keep their Rayleigh scores; the mask is chosen per test.
checks.reason: psi_L^2>=c0^2 L^-d on B_L, and m_R=1 on supp psi_L (inside B_2L, inside B_R), so V=h there. Tonelli gives int_{B_L}Gamma*q=int q(y)Gamma(B_L-y)dy. For |y|<=A<=L/2, B_{L/2} lies inside B_L-y, and Gamma(B_{L/2})=(L/2)^{d-alpha}Gamma(B1). So C_G=c0^2 2^{alpha-d}Gamma(B1)int q_avg, which is exact. alpha<2 follows from alpha+a<2 with a>0, so a finite L gives eps_R>0 for every sigma. The order is right: R is fixed first, then the generic theorem gives lambda>=sqrt(eps_R), and only then (4) gives |lambda_sigma-lambda_tau|<=dV/(2sqrt(eps_R)). lambda_0>0 because h_0>=Gamma*q_avg. Enlarging the mask leaves (26) and int h g^2 unchanged on covered supports. No uniform mask over a class of tests and no interchange of limits is asserted.

minor: Section 5 asserts that formula (14) solves the full-F Duhamel equation 'by variation of constants', but does not display the Fubini rearrangement. That rearrangement shows P^E(t)e plus the integral of P^E(t-r)g(r) dr satisfies Y=S_E e+int S_E(t-r)(B^E Y+g). I checked the identity and it holds; writing out the one-line computation would close the step on the page.

Section 2 identifies the form domain of H_sigma with H1 via Riesz plus elliptic regularity. It implicitly uses the standard form/operator correspondence (Kato representation theorem: D((H+c)^{1/2}) equals the closed-form domain, with H2 a core). This is standard but is not named as an import.

Section 4 uses the free wave group on H1xL2, with generator domain H2xH1, for the product-rule differentiation. Only S_E on E is an accepted named input; the H1xL2 restriction follows from the same Fourier multipliers but is not stated.

The accepted physical flow is constructed on a fixed horizon T, while (12), (13), (17) and (19) are asserted for all t>=0. Consistency across horizons follows from Duhamel uniqueness, but is left implicit.
Section 7 uses Q_0=||q_avg||_2^2>0 and int q_avg>0 without saying why q_avg is nonzero. This is immediate from int q_avg=int int Psi>0 for nonnegative nonzero Psi.
Section 7 wording: 'No global decay or translation bound on Gamma*h is used' should presumably say 'on h_sigma' or 'on Gamma*Psi'.
Section 4 only says the decaying-branch projection is uniformly bounded. Its explicit formula (<p,u>-<p,z>/lambda)/2 times (p,-lambda p) is not displayed. It is easy to verify.

Real-subspace restriction of the complex functional calculus is only implied by the conjugation remark in Section 2. C_t and S_t are real even functions of a real operator, so they preserve real phases; one sentence would make this explicit.

Section 9 says F1-F4 'would provide the exact deterministic indexed-family cone inputs on the ACCEPTED F'. The cone proof itself was done on the old uniformly-local d1 F, with e0=(1,0) and J without the c1 term. Re-establishing the cone on the new F, with O_phi and e0=(0,1,0), remains a downstream obligation. The candidate frames this conditionally and correctly.
